key_insight: Medical multimodal LLMs can sound confident even when they are wrong, and this paper shows that calibration can be improved with a domain-specific interrogation-and-assessment approach.
clinical_relevance: Better confidence calibration may make AI-assisted medical VQA more trustworthy by helping clinicians interpret model answers with appropriate caution.
method: Multi-Strategy Fusion-Based Interrogation (MS-FBI) to probe model confidence from multiple prompts/angles
Auxiliary expert LLM assessment to refine confidence estimates
Calibration-focused evaluation using Expected Calibration Error (ECE)
evidence_signal: Across three Medical VQA datasets, the proposed method reduced ECE by an average of 40%, indicating substantially better alignment between confidence and correctness.
watch_item: Improved calibration does not guarantee clinical correctness, so real-world deployment still needs careful validation, monitoring, and human oversight.
paper_title: Confidence Calibration for Multimodal LLMs: An Empirical Study through Medical VQA
